title: Borrowing: &, &mut and slices
hints: Look at the README's 'New syntax' table. Every function here *borrows*: it never owns its input, so nothing is moved or freed. `sum` and `double_all` are `for` loops; `first_word` and `trim_zeros` return slices of their input.

Ideas: `sum` adds up each `x` (a `&i64`: `total += x` works through the reference); `double_all` loops with `.iter_mut()` and writes through `*x`; `first_word` finds the first space and slices up to it (or returns all of `s`); `trim_zeros` moves a `start` index forward and an `end` index back past zeros, then returns `&xs[start..end]`; `log_twice` pushes `line.to_string()` twice.

E0499/E0502 ('cannot borrow as mutable because it is also borrowed') means two borrows overlap. E0308 'expected `&str`, found `String`' usually means you built a new String where a borrow of the input was asked for: slice the input instead.

Same shapes on other data: `let mut best = 0; for p in prices { best += p; }` · `for c in counts.iter_mut() { *c = 0; }` · `&line[..line.find('#').unwrap_or(line.len())]` (drop a comment) · `while end > 0 && bytes[end - 1] == b' ' { end -= 1; }`
